Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one alternate player-level follow-camera conceptual still for a playful freely explorable portfolio game world, landscape 1536 x 1024 pixels.

Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and strict spatial, character, architecture, color, and art-style reference. Produce one camera-change edit of this SAME WORLD. Retain the painted, simplified LOW-POLY GAME ART. This is NOT a photograph or a realistic wooden diorama render.

Primary request: Move the camera and the existing small wooden character together to the LEFT side of the level, beside the blue marble and marble track. The camera is now immediately behind the same character, around its shoulder-to-head height, looking diagonally inward toward the central layered hill and the workshop behind it. The character is seen from behind, lower middle of frame, approximately 15 percent of the frame height, still the faceted warm-brown wooden head/hair, charcoal knitted-looking simplified jacket, olive trousers, brown boots from the reference. Have it stand beside the blue marble, not inside or blocked by the track. This should clearly feel like a third-person playable view reached by walking across the pictured world, rather than another high overview.

Preserve exact environment and relative layout: the broad open plywood ground on a large workbench; the open-front workshop in the rear left with green doors, warm timber, desktop monitor, keyboard, breadboard electronics and stool; the low central layered round hill with green tops, broad front ramp, little windmill and trees; the round-window timber room in the rear right with green framing, roof terrace, a climbable broad side ramp, blue bird and plant; the connecting plank bridge from central hill to that accessible roof; the smaller game shed at front right with a screen; the curved wooden marble track on the left with blue marble. From the new camera, the marble and track should be close on the left, workshop visible left of center farther away, low hill prominent center-right, round-window room and roof beyond it on the right. The small game shed can be cropped at the far right foreground or partly occluded as proper perspective requires. Keep all structural locations and construction believable, without rearranging the world just to expose every object.

Free movement must read clearly from geometry: wide uncluttered open ground goes around BOTH sides of the low hill, ground reaches the workshop doorway, a simple broad ramp rises onto the hill, and the plank and side ramp make the roof accessible. Maintain player-scale clearances. No fenced funnel, forced trail, waypoint route, or isolated point-to-point stations. No path arrows painted on the floor.

Style: joyful small handmade toy world, simple chunky geometry, flat painted surfaces, restrained soft shadows, faceted foliage and rocks, coherent warm timber/green painted wood colors from the reference. Reduce fine wood grain and surface noise; keep a stylized interactive-game screenshot appearance and a warm workshop backdrop rendered equally simply. No photoreal depth of field or macro photography. No abandoned or dusty theme.

Main UI only: tiny clean white text "Storm Selvig" at top left, "Index" at top right, and "WASD / arrows — move    Drag — look" at bottom left. A tiny optional contextual prompt "E — push" can sit near the blue marble. Do not include any other UI text except the existing small physical Work workshop sign if naturally visible. No hotspot dots, destination labels, numbered stations, arrows, quest markers, navigation trail, color palette, presentation annotations, comparison panels, marketing headings, or webpage cards. One coherent image, no border.
